items.stem: You must look up a price using a key that sits to the right of the return column, on unsorted data. Which approach is most reliable?

options.text: XLOOKUP, or INDEX/MATCH, both of which look up in any direction
options.rationale: Correct: neither requires the return column to be to the right, and both default to exact match.

options.text: VLOOKUP, which can look to the left
options.rationale: VLOOKUP cannot return a column to the left of the key.
HLOOKUP is for horizontal data and approximate match misfires on unsorted data.

options.text: A manual sort then VLOOKUP approximate
options.rationale: That is fragile and still cannot look left.

items.explanation: Correct: neither requires the return column to be to the right, and both default to exact match.

items.stem: Which TWO statements about dynamic-array formulas are correct? (Select TWO.)

options.text: FILTER returns a spilling result that resizes as source data changes
options.rationale: Correct: dynamic arrays spill and recalculate automatically.

options.text: You can reference a spill range with the # operator, e.g. A2#
options.rationale: Correct: the # suffix refers to the whole spilled range.

options.text: Dynamic arrays require pressing Ctrl+Shift+Enter like legacy arrays
options.rationale: Modern dynamic arrays spill automatically with a normal Enter.

options.text: A #SPILL! error means the formula syntax is wrong
options.rationale: #SPILL! means the output range is blocked, not that the syntax is invalid.

items.explanation: Correct: dynamic arrays spill and recalculate automatically.

items.stem: A formula shows #SPILL!. What is the correct first step?

options.text: Clear the cells blocking the spill range below or beside the formula
options.rationale: Correct: #SPILL! occurs when something obstructs where the array needs to expand.

options.text: Wrap the formula in IFERROR to hide it
options.rationale: That conceals the problem without resolving the blockage.

options.text: Convert the workbook to an older format
options.rationale: File format is not the cause.
The formula is valid; only the spill area must be cleared.

items.explanation: Correct: #SPILL! occurs when something obstructs where the array needs to expand.
